title: Higher order derivatives
goal: Understand what the derivative of the derivative ($f''$) tells you: while $f'$ measures how steep the hill is, $f''$ measures whether the hill is curving upward or downward.

beforeThis.skill: Think of driving a car: $f(t)$ is your position on the road, $f'(t)$ is your speedometer (velocity), and $f''(t)$ is how hard you press the gas or brake pedal (acceleration).

seeIt.title: Concavity & The Second Derivative
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Shows how the sign of $f''(x)$ tells you whether the slope $f'(x)$ is increasing (concave up) or decreasing (concave down).

slowWalkthrough.title: Calculus 1 Lecture 2.4: Applications of the Derivative
slowWalkthrough.creator: Professor Leonard

questions.asking: Spot which of the five graphs goes downward from left to right while its tangent slope becomes less negative (bends upward) on $(a, b)$.
questions.statement: A function $f(x)$ satisfies $f'(x) < 0$ and $f''(x) > 0$ over $(a, b)$. Which of the following curves below might represent $y = f(x)$?

figures.alt: Five small graphs labeled (i) through (v) over the interval (a, b): (i) increasing and bending upward; (ii) decreasing and bending upward; (iii) decreasing and bending downward; (iv) increasing and bending downward; (v) decreasing straight line.
